4488.title: [WASM] Add preview-.NET WASM test job to catch exception-handling regressions
4488.body:
[WASM] Add preview-.NET WASM test job to catch exception-handling regressions (#4488)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4487

The emsdk 5.0.6 WASM libSkiaSharp can emit *legacy* wasm exception-handling
instructions, while .NET 11 links Blazor WASM apps with the *new* exnref model
(WASM_LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS=0). Mixing the two makes the app fail at runtime in the
browser, before a single line of user code runs:

    CompileError: WebAssembly.compileStreaming(): module uses a mix of legacy
    and new exception handling instructions

PR #4487 fixes the native build to emit new-EH instructions, but nothing in CI
would have caught the original regression. This adds that missing guard: it runs
the existing tests/SkiaSharp.Tests.Wasm suite under the preview .NET (net11) so an
EH mismatch — or any WASM breakage on the newer runtime — turns the build red.

The preview runtime is used for TESTS ONLY. net10 remains the default for every
other job, and the shipping TFMs are unchanged.

  * source/SkiaSharp.Build.props: add an opt-in UsePreviewTFM toggle (default
    off) that shifts the .NET version window forward one release (current=net11,
    previous=net10). Dropping the now-EOL net9.0 lets the test and the SkiaSharp
    binding it references build cleanly as net11.0 under a preview SDK, without
    tripping NETSDK1202 on the EOL net9.0-* platform TFMs.
  * scripts/infra/tests/tests-wasm.cake: add --previewtfm=true, which runs the
    same suite with -p:UsePreviewTFM=true. The cake is the run, not the infra.
  * scripts/azure-templates-jobs-bootstrapper.yml: add reusable installPreviewSdk
    and previewWorkloads parameters (install the preview SDK, pin global.json to
    it, install the requested workloads via the shared install-dotnet-workloads.ps1
    at the exact preview workload set) so other jobs can opt into a preview run.
  * scripts/azure-templates-variables.yml: add DOTNET_VERSION_PREVIEW and
    DOTNET_WORKLOAD_VERSION_PREVIEW (default DOTNET_VERSION stays net10).
  * scripts/azure-templates-stages-test.yml: add the tests_wasm_preview_linux job
    (consumes the native artifact; previewWorkloads=wasm-tools,android). android
    is required because the WASM restore still evaluates the -android TFMs of the
    referenced binding projects, exactly as the net10 job already does.

Both paths were validated locally against real 5.0.6/st,simd natives pulled from
CI artifacts: the new-EH lib runs the suite green (1180 total, 1081 passed, 0
failed, 99 skipped), and the legacy-EH lib fails with the CompileError above and
takes the job red via the runner's 300s timeout — a bounded failure, not a hang
or a silent pass.

Note: the preview .NET workload set, its manifests, and the emscripten 5.0.6 and
android packs are not on the dnceng public feeds by default (preview/late-leg
builds move to internal feeds), so the exact pinned versions were mirrored to
dotnet-public to make the pinned install reproducible in CI.

4370.title: [performance] Port SKColor -> SKColorF conversion to managed C#
4370.body:
Port SKColor -> SKColorF conversion to managed C# (#4370)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4369

The implicit SKColor -> SKColorF conversion is pure per-channel math
(each 8-bit channel * 1/255, no gamma), yet every call crossed the
managed->native boundary via the sk_color4f_from_color P/Invoke - plus,
on the dynamic-load path, a cached-delegate indirection - and pinned an
output pointer. Because it is an implicit operator it is hit inside
per-item / per-frame loops: e.g. SKRuntimeEffect converts SKColor ->
SKColorF when setting a colour uniform, so an animated shader pays the
transition every frame.

Reimplement the operator in managed code as `channel * (1f/255f)` per
channel, marked AggressiveInlining. This removes the P/Invoke, the
delegate indirection and the pointer pin from a hot path. The operator
signature and public surface are unchanged, so there is no ABI break -
this is an internal implementation swap.

Faster (CI, BenchmarkDotNet 0.14, .NET 10), tracked via
ColorMathBenchmark.ToColorF (4096 colours through this operator),
PR build (managed) vs the previous released package (native):

  * Linux X64     12.7 us vs 20.6 us   ~1.6x   (0 B / 0 B)
  * Windows X64   13.6 us vs 25.6 us   ~1.9x   (0 B / 0 B)
  * macOS Arm64    5.1 us vs 12.9 us   ~2.5x   (0 B / 0 B)

Zero allocations before and after; the standalone SKColorFConvertBenchmark
(New vs Old) shows the same ~2x per-call win.

Behaviour-identical (bit-exact). SKColorFConvertEquivalenceTest compares
the managed operator against the native sk_color4f_from_color oracle by
reinterpreting the raw float bits (exact bits, not a tolerance) across all
256 grayscale values, each channel swept 0-255 with the others held
distinct (catches a swapped-channel port), and the 0/255 extremes, plus a
guard proving the comparison rejects both a swapped-R/B result and a naive
`x/255f`. The single-multiply-per-channel formula is bit-identical on every
runtime including x86 x87 (the 48-bit product fits the 64-bit extended
mantissa, so no double-rounding), verified on both the x64 (SSE) and x86
(x87) .NET Framework legs.

The reverse operator (SKColorF -> SKColor) is deliberately left native:
it is clamp -> *255 -> +0.5 -> floor, several dependent float ops that can
differ by 1 ULP under x87 extended precision, so a safe managed port would
need a native-math fallback and is a colder path - out of scope here.
ColorMathBenchmark.ToColor stays as a native sentinel so a future managed
regression would surface as a diverging ToColorF/ToColor ratio.

The equivalence test originally used BitConverter.SingleToInt32Bits, which
does not exist on .NET Framework, breaking the net48 test leg's compile;
it now uses an unsafe float->int32 reinterpret that is bit-identical on
every runtime.

4385.title: Port single-value SKPMColor premultiply/unpremultiply to managed integer math
4385.body:
Port single-value SKPMColor premultiply/unpremultiply to managed integer math (#4385)

SKPMColor.PreMultiply(SKColor) and UnPreMultiply(SKPMColor) each round-tripped
a single colour through a native P/Invoke (sk_color_premultiply /
sk_color_unpremultiply) even though the underlying work is only a handful of
integer ops. Callers that convert one colour at a time — gradient ramps, palette
expansion, per-pixel software blends — hit these in tight loops, so the managed
to native transition cost dominated the actual conversion.

Reimplement both in managed C# using Skia's exact integer algorithms, so the
result is bit-exact with the native path for every input:

  * PreMultiply uses SkMulDiv255Round(c, a) = (p + (p >> 8)) >> 8, p = c*a + 128,
    per channel, with the opaque (a == 255) case passing through unchanged.
  * UnPreMultiply mirrors SkUnPreMultiply::gTable — a 256-entry
    round((255 << 24) / a) scale table built once at type init — then applies
    ApplyScale(scale, c) = (scale*c + (1 << 23)) >> 24, turning a per-call 32-bit
    divide into a table lookup.

The maths is integer-only, so it stays deterministic across all runtimes and
TFMs (no x87/float divergence, unlike float ports such as #4241) and matches the
native uint32 wrap even for out-of-gamut premultiplied colours where a channel
exceeds alpha. Only the method bodies change, so this is ABI-safe: the array
overloads stay native (already one P/Invoke per batch) and the cast operators are
untouched — both call these two methods, so they benefit automatically.

Correctness is proven, not assumed. SKPMColorEquivalenceTest exhaustively sweeps
alpha 0..255 x channel 0..255 for each R/G/B position against the native oracle
(sk_color_(un)premultiply) — a complete enumeration of every reachable input —
with distinct sentinels pinning the packing order, an opaque round-trip check,
and deliberately-wrong "teeth" guards proving the oracle comparison actually
detects divergence.

The Track - Benchmarks CI (ColorMathBenchmark) confirms the win with zero
allocations on every leg, managed vs the still-native nightly baseline on the
same runners:

  * Linux:   PreMultiply +32.9%, UnPreMultiply +31.6%
  * Windows: PreMultiply +24.1%, UnPreMultiply +20.9%
  * macOS:   PreMultiply +12.3%, UnPreMultiply  +2.4%

This also lays to rest the earlier "Linux regression" concern, which was
runner/baseline noise — Linux in fact benefits the most.

4487.title: [WASM] Build emsdk 5.0.6 libs with new exnref exception handling
4487.body:
[WASM] Build emsdk 5.0.6 libs with new exnref exception handling (#4487)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4459

A .NET 11 Blazor WebAssembly app that references SkiaSharp links fine but
fails at runtime in a modern browser while instantiating the module:

    CompileError: WebAssembly.compileStreaming(): module uses a mix of
    legacy and new exception handling instructions (function #19801)

.NET 11 (preview 6+) links WASM apps with the *new* wasm exception-handling
model (exnref: WASM_LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS=0, emitting try_table/throw_ref).
#4459 correctly started shipping an emsdk 5.0.6 static library so net11.0+
apps link against a matching toolchain, but that library was still compiled
with only -fwasm-exceptions and no instruction-variant pin, so it emitted the
*legacy* wasm-EH instructions (try/catch). V8 refuses to compile a module that
mixes the two schemes, hence the CompileError. #4459 fixed the earlier link
failure; this fixes the remaining runtime EH mismatch.

Add a `_newexc` emscripten feature to native/wasm/build.cake that appends
`-s WASM_LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS=0` to both extra_cflags and extra_cflags_cc. This
is a codegen-affecting flag that must be passed at compile time (the .a build
produces wasm object files, so codegen happens during compile, not link), and
it has to cover both the C++ exceptions and the wasm setjmp/longjmp used by the
C dependencies (libjpeg-turbo, libpng, etc.). Enable the feature only on the
four 5.0.6 native matrix variants (st / mt / simd / simd+mt) in
scripts/azure-templates-stages-native-wasm.yml.

net8 (emsdk 3.1.34) and net9/net10 (emsdk 3.1.56) keep the legacy EH model to
match their runtimes, which predate the exnref proposal, so their build paths
are byte-identical (the flag is only added when `_newexc` is present). No
packaging or lib-selection changes are needed: `_`-prefixed feature tokens are
excluded from the artifact path, and the net11.0+ -> 5.0.6 selection already
exists from #4459.

Verified by rebuilding the 5.0.6 st and st,simd libraries from source: the
rebuilt .a disassembles to the new try_table/throw_ref instructions with no
legacy try-block/delegate/rethrow, and a net11.0 Blazor WASM app that failed
with the CompileError on the shipped (legacy-EH) lib now boots and renders with
SkiaSharp. net10 continues to link the legacy EH path (-lc++-except, no
-wasm-use-legacy-eh=0) and is unaffected.

4480.title: Expand SKMatrix tracking benchmarks for the managed-port surface (#4241)
4480.body:
The tracking suite only measured SKMatrix.MapPoints (the batch overload), which
is the weakest indicator of the managed SKMatrix port in #4241: the batch does a
single native call for the whole array, so the per-call P/Invoke that #4241
removes is amortised to almost nothing. The single-op operations - where the
managed<->native transition is paid on every call - are where that win actually
shows, and they had no permanent coverage.

Split the SKMatrix surface into two tracked groups, mirroring how #4241 changes it:

  * MatrixMapPointsBenchmark (expanded, geometry mapping) - add MapPoint, MapRect,
    MapVector and MapRadius, each looped over the existing deterministic point set.
    The pre-existing MapPoints method and its Points params are left untouched (a
    shipped history key must never be renamed). All the new methods are
    allocation-free; MapPoints keeps its allocating batch behaviour as a signal.
  * MatrixOpsBenchmark (new, matrix algebra) - Concat (pre + post multiply) and
    Invert, the operations that produce another matrix rather than mapping geometry.

Local short-run against the 4.151 nightly shows the single-op methods are dominated
by interop overhead (MapPoint 24.6 us vs the MapPoints batch 1.88 us for the same
4096 points; MapRect 55 us, MapRadius 118 us, Concat 125 us, Invert 71 us) - all
zero-alloc - so #4241 should visibly drop their time lines while the batch barely
moves. The operands are affine (rotation/scale/translate), which is #4241's managed
fast path; perspective would fall back to native. Public API only, deterministic
(fixed seed), and verified to compile against both the 3.119.4 baseline and 4.151
nightly (no new #if needed).

4428.title: Restore SK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT to fix CPU raster regression
4428.body:
Restore SK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT to fix CPU raster regression (#4428)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4421
Context: https://skia.googlesource.com/skia/+/356c7267fa (Remove SK_DISABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT)
Context: https://skia.googlesource.com/skia/+/1a15ed6b17 (Allow users to set SK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT)
Related: #4463 (benchmark native cache-key fix), #4465 (LargeImageScaleBenchmark)

Starting with Skia milestone m146, software (CPU) rasterization of scaled or
tiled bitmaps regressed badly — high CPU, frame drops, and flicker that made
SKCanvasView nearly unusable on Windows. As diagnosed in #4421 by @janne-hmp,
upstream commit 356c7267fa dropped the default definition of
SK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT from include/core/SkTypes.h. With the macro
undefined, SkShaderBase::makeContext() returns nullptr, so for kN32 + SrcOver
draws that carry a shader (a scaled/tiled bitmap builds a sampling shader)
SkBlitter::Choose can no longer use the hand-tuned SkARGB32_Shader_Blitter and
falls back to the generic raster-pipeline blitter for every draw.

The same upstream change (1a15ed6b17) deliberately made the macro user-settable
before removing its default, so defining it in the build is the sanctioned way
to restore the previous behaviour rather than a workaround.

Add -DSK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT to extra_cflags, alongside the existing
SK_AVOID_SLOW_RASTER_PIPELINE_BLURS perf flag, in every CPU-raster libSkiaSharp
build (windows, macos, ios, tvos, linux, android, tizen, wasm; maccatalyst,
nanoserver and linuxnodeps inherit via delegation). This restores the exact
pre-m146 default across all platforms. winui (WinRT projection) and winui-angle
(ANGLE GL) are unaffected and left alone.

Verified two ways: @janne-hmp confirmed the PR artifacts resolve the regression
in their app, and a new regression benchmark (LargeImageScaleBenchmark, #4465 —
made measurable on CI by the native cache-key fix in #4463) shows the isolated
scaled-image path is 3x faster on macOS, ~5x on Windows, and up to ~18x on Linux
with the define restored. The raster-pipeline path is also notably load-sensitive
run-to-run, which matches the sustained-load throttling reported in #4421.

Note: SK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT is legacy upstream and will eventually be
removed, so this restores prior behaviour rather than guaranteeing it long-term;
the underlying raster-pipeline image-sampling gap is being raised on skia-discuss.

4476.title: Add regression-tracking benchmarks for common colour/interop paths
4476.body:
Add regression-tracking benchmarks for common colour/interop paths (#4476)

Derived from: #4370, #4385, #4442, #4453, #4455
CI: Track - Benchmarks run 29608575980 (green, all OS/roles)

The permanent regression-tracking suite (SkiaSharp.Benchmarks.Tracking) landed
recently alongside a wave of perf/agentic PRs, but it had no coverage for the
managed colour/interop paths those PRs actually touch. This adds a small,
curated set of trackers so a future regression (or the improvement itself) shows
up as a step in the persisted per-OS time/allocation history.

Following the suite's scaled-pyramid philosophy (a few small common-path trackers
plus one broad composite, not a micro-benchmark per PR), four benchmarks are
added under Tracking/Benchmarks/ (auto-linked into the source-mode project, so
they also drive the PR column):

  * ColorMathBenchmark - managed SKColor->SKColorF (#4370) and SKPMColor
    PreMultiply/UnPreMultiply (#4385). Zero-alloc; the ToColorF/ToColor ratio
    (the reverse operator stays native) is a managed-regression signal even on
    noisy shared runners. These two ports are the real, dashboard-visible speed
    wins - their time lines should drop when the ports merge.
  * RasterImageLifecycleBenchmark - create+dispose churn of SKImage.Create raster
    (#4455) and SKData.Create with a managed release proc (#4453). Allocation is
    the tracked signal for that object-lifecycle area.
  * RuntimeEffectShaderBenchmark - a per-frame animated SkSL shader: build
    uniforms (the SKColor uniform pays the #4370 convert), ToShader, draw. Covers
    the uniforms lifecycle whose SKData leak #4442 touched.
  * SceneRenderBenchmark - one broad frame (transforms, linear+radial gradients,
    filled/stroked primitives, a built path, a scaled image draw, a colour-filter
    layer, clipping, managed colour maths) so many unrelated future optimizations
    each nudge it - a merge indicator rather than a micro-benchmark.

Scope notes: the failure-path leak fixes (#4453, #4455), the native uniforms leak
(#4442), and the UAF/double-free fixes (#4372, #4468) are correctness/native-memory
changes that a throughput + managed-allocation dashboard largely will not register;
they are represented here by area, not as leak assertions (those belong in soak/
leak tests). #4372 and #4468 are intentionally not benchmarked (niche debug canvases;
HarfBuzz lives in a separate assembly the tracking project does not reference).

All benchmarks use public API only (the project references the nightly NuGet, not
internal SkiaApi), are deterministic and machine-independent (fixed seeds, no fonts
or external content), and compile against every benchmarked role - verified against
the 3.119.4 baseline (prev-major) and 4.151 nightly, with only SKPath/SKPathBuilder
behind the existing #if. A short local run and the full CI matrix (Linux/Windows/
macOS, all version roles plus the source-built PR column) emit time and allocation
data for every case.

4477.title: Add chart time-window and smoothing-span controls to the perf dashboard
4477.body:
The tracker now records several points per day (6-hourly), so the perf
dashboard needed controls to focus on a slice of history and to smooth
over a sensible amount of time rather than a fixed run count.

Chart header:
- Window pill (1d/7d/30d/60d/120d/All, default 30d): clips the plotted
  trend to points within N days of the most recent run (anchored to the
  data, not wall-clock, so an older embedded snapshot still shows a
  sensible window). Baselines are unaffected.
- Both header groups (Window, Scale) now have small-caps headings that
  match the top toolbar (Metric/Group/OS/etc.).

Smoothing:
- New Span pill (1d/3d/7d, default 3d) sets the median window used by the
  smoothed chart line AND the Status column. The window is now TIME-based
  (median over runs within N days) instead of a fixed 7-point count, so it
  stays meaningful at any cadence and handles the mixed legacy-daily /
  new-6-hourly history correctly. Default 3d is ~12 runs at the 6h cadence
  — steady enough to average across the varying runner hardware while still
  reacting to a real shift within a couple of days.
- Smoothing On/Off keeps its meaning (denoise the chart line + headline
  number); Span is separate because the window is used by the Status
  column regardless of that toggle.

Usability:
- Descriptive title tooltips on every pill header and every option
  (including the dynamically-rendered Group and OS chips), plus Clear and
  the search box.
- Chart tooltip now shows HH:MM for intraday points (date-only for legacy
  midnight points).

4459.title: [WASM] Add Emscripten 5.0.6 static libraries for .NET 11
4459.body:
[WASM] Add Emscripten 5.0.6 static libraries for .NET 11 (#4459)

.NET 11 (preview 6+) links WASM apps with emsdk 5.0.6, replacing the 3.x
toolchain used by .NET 9/10. The buildTransitive targets selected the native
static library with an open-ended `net9.0+` -> Emscripten 3.1.56 rule, so a
net11.0 app was handed the 3.1.56 libSkiaSharp.a. A static library built with
Emscripten 3.x cannot be linked by emsdk 5.x (incompatible wasm object format),
producing a link failure.

Selection logic evaluated per TFM before the fix:

    | App TFM | emsdk the SDK links with | lib selected | result       |
    |---------|--------------------------|--------------|--------------|
    | net8.0  | 3.1.34                   | 3.1.34       | ok           |
    | net9.0  | 3.1.56                   | 3.1.56       | ok           |
    | net10.0 | 3.1.56                   | 3.1.56       | ok           |
    | net11.0 | 5.0.6                    | 3.1.56       | link failure |

Split the open-ended rule into bounded ranges and add a net11.0+ -> 5.0.6 entry,
wiring the new Emscripten version through the build and merge pipeline so the
packages actually ship it:

  * Consumer targets (shipped): SkiaSharp/HarfBuzzSharp NativeAssets.WebAssembly
    buildTransitive targets now route net9.0-net10.x -> 3.1.56, net11.0+ -> 5.0.6.
  * Repo-internal build/test: IncludeNativeAssets.{SkiaSharp,HarfBuzzSharp}.targets
    mirror the same split.
  * CI: add the four 5.0.6 variants (st/mt/simd/simd+mt) to the WASM build matrix
    and register the native_wasm_5_0_6_* artifacts in both native-merge lists.
  * Docs: update packages.md and updating-dotnet-version.md (remove the now-false
    ">=9.0 covers future versions" note; document the emsdk-per-SDK mapping).

Packaging globs (** / * over the version folder) pick up the new 5.0.6/
directory automatically, so no nuspec/csproj change is needed, and the WASM
Docker image already installs whatever EMSCRIPTEN_VERSION is passed.

The newest entry is intentionally left open-ended (net11.0+). net9.0 and net10.0
already share 3.1.56, and .NET 12+ may keep 5.0.6, so a future SDK that reuses
the same toolchain works with no code change. An entry is only capped with an
upper bound once a new SDK actually diverges (as net9.0-net10.x was capped at
< net11.0 when .NET 11 moved to 5.0.6). This convention is documented in
updating-dotnet-version.md.

4473.title: Add robust smoothing + regression Status to the perf dashboard
4473.body:
The perf dashboard plotted raw benchmark points and computed the grid delta
by comparing a single latest point to a baseline against a flat percentage
threshold. Time benchmarks on the shared CI runners carry ~9-11% between-run
jitter (BenchmarkDotNet's within-run stdDev is <0.5%), so that point-vs-baseline
rule fired on ~53% of steps in the live nightly history — pure noise, and easy
to mistake for real movement. Allocations and size are deterministic, so they
never had this problem and must keep showing any change exactly.

Add an optional, robust denoising layer that separates *display smoothing* from
*change detection*, applied per metric:

* Chart (Smoothing on): faint raw points stay visible under a rolling-median
  trend (7-run window), plus a translucent +/-3*MAD band on single selection.
* Grid: a new Status column (always shown, every metric) reports the robust
  verdict — stable / regressed / improved / noisy / — by comparing the last

4469.title: Track benchmarks every 6h with per-run datetime data points
4469.body:
Track benchmarks every 6h with per-run datetime data points (#4469)

The benchmark tracker (track-benchmarks.yml) ran once a day and stored at
most one point per day: track.py keyed each point by YYYY-MM-DD and
overwrote it on re-run, so even multiple runs a day collapsed to a single
data point. That gave a coarse trend and no way to see intra-day or
environment-driven variation.

Move the schedule to a plain 6-hour cadence (cron "0 8 * * *" ->
"0 */6 * * *") and record a fresh point on every run. A run is cheap
(~13-15 min) and we *want* to capture runner/environment variation, so the
per-leg "freshness" skip (and its version+source fingerprint gate) is
removed entirely -- every (OS, role) leg now runs and records each time.

To make more frequent points meaningful, loosen the point key from a date
to a full ISO-8601 UTC datetime (the existing `date` field, same name).
Each run becomes its own point; an idempotent re-run at the same timestamp
still replaces in place. Retention becomes age-based (MAX_AGE_DAYS = 365)
instead of a fixed count, so the schedule can be sped up or slowed down
arbitrarily without shrinking the retained time window. The dashboard's
x-axis is already type:"time"; loosening the single dateMs parser to accept
a datetime is enough for it to render hours, and render_md labels nightly
columns MM-DD HH:MM. The size tracker (date-only) is unaffected via the
same parser's fallback.

~~ Recorded fingerprint + host environment ~~

The fingerprint was previously only used to skip unchanged runs. Rather
than drop it with the skip, keep it as recorded (non-gating) metadata:
each point stores `fingerprint = version | hash(benchmark source)`. A perf
change with an unchanged fingerprint points at the environment; a changed
fingerprint means the code or version moved. Each point also records an
`env` block pulled from the BenchmarkDotNet report's HostEnvironmentInfo
(CPU, physical/logical cores, arch, OS, runtime, .NET SDK, BDN version).
Both fields flow through merge_summaries into index.json and the
dashboard's embedded data; the renderers ignore them for now, so surfacing
an "environment changed" indicator is a self-contained follow-up. No RAM
is recorded (BDN does not report it).

Legacy date-only points already on the aw-data branch coexist and render
with no migration; merge_summaries.py, persist-aw-data.yml, and the
artifact-size tracker are untouched.

Validated on two full Track - Benchmarks runs against this PR: resolve, all
15 benchmark legs, all 3 PR source-build legs, and report were green.
Downloaded artifacts confirmed real points with datetime keys, a
fingerprint, and a full env block; the runner CPU actually varied across
runs (Intel Xeon 8370C / AMD EPYC 9V74 / Intel Xeon 6973P-C), exactly the
infra variation the env block now captures. One report run hit a transient
actions/download-artifact@v4 403 (GitHub infra, unrelated to this change);
a re-run and the next full run both passed.

4463.title: Fix benchmark -pr column silently downloading nightly for cflags-only PRs
4463.body:
The `benchmark-source` job's "Decide native build mode" step used the coarse
parent `--job native` repo-deps cache-key to decide, in "auto" mode, whether the
-pr column builds libSkiaSharp from source or downloads the prebuilt nightly.

The parent `native` job key only hashes `scripts/infra/native/shared/**` plus the
`externals/skia` + `externals/depot_tools` submodule SHAs. The per-platform
`native/<plat>/build.cake` files — which hold `extra_cflags` — live in the job's
CHILDREN (native/linux, native/macos, native/windows), and the parent key never
descends into children. So a flag-only native change (e.g. adding a `-D` define to
extra_cflags) produced an identical HEAD-vs-main key, "auto" concluded native was
unchanged, and the -pr leg downloaded the define-OFF nightly instead of building
this branch — a meaningless define-OFF vs define-OFF A/B.

Use each leg's per-platform CHILD job (new `matrix.nativeJob`:
native/linux|macos|windows) for both cache-key invocations (HEAD and the main
worktree). The child key is a strict superset of the parent — same shared files and
submodule SHAs, plus `native/<plat>/**` + `scripts/infra/native/<plat>/**` — so
nothing is lost and flag-only native changes now correctly trigger the source build.

Motivating case: #4421 / #4428 (adds -DSK_ENABLE_LEGACY_SHADERCONTEXT to extra_cflags).

so shipped packages rebuilt correctly; only this benchmark workflow used the parent key.

4449.title: Automate issue-template version dropdowns via a daily refresh workflow
4449.body:
Automate issue-template version dropdowns via a daily refresh workflow (#4449)

The SkiaSharp version pickers in the bug-report issue form were maintained
by hand and had drifted badly — both the "Version of SkiaSharp" and "Last
Known Good Version of SkiaSharp" dropdowns were still frozen on the retired
3.116/3.118 line, long after the 4.x series shipped. A stale New Issue page
means every bug report starts with wrong version options.

Replace the manual edits with a small generator plus a scheduled workflow so
the lists track what actually ships:

  * scripts/infra/milestones/update-bug-template.py regenerates both
    dropdowns from the published GitHub Releases (the source of truth for
    what a user can install). The supported major comes from
    scripts/VERSIONS.txt; older majors collapse to a single "N.x (Obsolete)"
    entry, since the triage answer for an unmaintained line is just "please
    update".
  * .github/workflows/auto-update-issue-template-versions.yml runs the
    generator daily at 09:00 UTC (and on workflow_dispatch) and opens or
    updates a PR whenever the dropdowns drift. Daily rather than weekly
    because releases can land late Friday / early Saturday, and a weekly cron
    could leave the form stale for days.
  * scripts/infra/milestones/README.md documents the generator alongside the
    existing milestone helpers (sync-chrome-milestones.ps1,
    audit-milestones.ps1).

The two dropdowns intentionally differ in how they treat the in-flight
release: "Version" lists only the newest pre-release build (a single
"Pre-release") plus a "Nightly / CI build" option, because when asking what
someone is on now the answer for an older preview is always "update". "Last
Known Good" lists every in-flight pre-release build individually, since a
regression may land between, say, preview.1 and preview.2 and pinpointing
that boundary is the whole point of the field.

This PR is deliberately tooling-only and does not touch bug-report.yml. The
actual dropdown refresh will arrive as a separate PR opened by the workflow
once it lives on the default branch — workflow_dispatch only fires from the
default branch, so the bot PR cannot be produced before merge. The generator
was simulated locally against the current stale template: it emits valid
YAML and git diff flags the change, so the first run (daily cron or a manual
dispatch after merge) will open the data PR.

4438.title: Add a cross-platform perf tracker: benchmarks, sizes, unified dashboard
4438.body:
Add a cross-platform perf-regression tracker: benchmarks, sizes, dashboard (#4438)

SkiaSharp had local benchmark tooling for one-off "old vs new" investigations
but no durable CI history. Once a performance PR merges, the old code is gone and
the new behaviour silently becomes the next baseline, so slow time/allocation
drift and native package-size growth were invisible across releases. This adds
continuous, persisted, cross-version tracking of benchmark time, allocations, and
NuGet/native artifact size, rendered as one interactive dashboard so regressions
surface instead of becoming the new normal. It is CI/tooling only — no existing
SkiaSharp library source is touched.

It also gives native regressions like #4421 a standing signal: the suite includes
a repro (BitmapDrawBenchmark, scaled vs unscaled DrawBitmap) whose ratio is a
hardware-independent indicator, so a platform hit by that shader-blitter fallback
stands out even before cross-OS normalization exists.

Version roles, split into released (on nuget.org) vs unreleased (CI/branch only):
  * nightly     -> newest -nightly.* on the EAP/CI feed (unreleased trend line)
  * latest      -> newest on nuget.org incl. preview/rc (released, still shipped)
  * curr/prev-stable, prev-major -> released stable baselines
  * pr          -> a source build of the branch (unreleased, ephemeral)
Benchmarks run Linux/Windows/macOS x the five roles; the pr source column runs
only on PR/dispatch (the nightly role already tracks main). The source build is
auto-gated on repo-deps.py's native cache-key: it only builds libSkiaSharp from
source when native inputs changed vs main, otherwise it downloads prebuilt
natives, keeping PR runs cheap.

Data model and persistence:
  * History lives on a dedicated aw-data git branch, not the Actions cache, so it
    survives for years. Each domain persists one merged summary the dashboard
    reads directly (benchmarks/index.json = {schema, legs}, sizes/index.json)
    plus additive plain-JSON raw captures under raw/<date>/... so summaries can be
    recomputed later. The ephemeral pr leg is dropped from persisted history.
  * The agent payload is uploaded on every run so any PR/dispatch run can download
    and preview exactly what would be persisted, but the actual commit to aw-data
    is gated in persist-aw-data.yml to successful same-repo runs whose head_branch
    is main. PR, branch, and fork runs never write to the branch; workflow_dispatch
    remains an admin override. Because this uses workflow_run (main's definition),
    persistence only begins after this PR merges and the first scheduled run lands.

Dashboard and tooling:
  * One ECharts page (scripts/infra/perf/templates/dashboard.html): metric tabs
    (Time/Allocations/Size), Absolute/Relative %/Log scales, searchable Group x
    Item multiselect, and a comparison table with PR / nightly / latest / stable
    columns. It ships as a self-contained per-run snapshot and also loads live
    from the aw-data raw URL, so the same file works locally, as an artifact, and
    against live history.
  * Shared tooling lives under scripts/infra/perf/ (_common.py for feed access and
    version-role resolution, merge_summaries.py, render_html.py, benchmarks/,
    sizes/, templates/). The size scripts moved here from .github/scripts/, and
    scripts/infra/perf/** is excluded in repo-deps.json since it is CI tooling with
    no effect on build caches (this also satisfies the public build's cache-config
    coverage validator).

Verified: both workflows green across all five roles on the three OSes plus the
source legs; the real agent payloads checked (benchmarks/index.json schema 2, 15
legs, no pr; sizes/index.json includes latest; raw is plain JSON); the
persist-aw-data copy/commit logic run against a real aw-data checkout adds
benchmarks/ and sizes/ additively without disturbing existing ai-triage data; and
the dashboard browser-verified rendering real data with distinct nightly and
latest columns.

3997.title: Fix native resource leak in SKImage.FromEncodedData(SKData, SKRectI)
3997.body:
Fix native resource leak in SKImage.FromEncodedData(SKData, SKRectI) (#3997)

The two-argument FromEncodedData(SKData, SKRectI) overload decoded an
intermediate full-size SKImage and then returned image.Subset(subset) via a
null-conditional one-liner:

    return FromEncodedData (data)?.Subset (subset);

When the requested subset is smaller than the full image, Subset() allocates a
new SkImage and returns a different wrapper, so the intermediate full-size image
was never disposed. Its native SkImage leaked until a GC eventually ran the
finalizer, which is exactly the case the same-instance disposal pattern used
elsewhere (ToRasterImage, other Subset call sites) exists to handle.

Apply that pattern: keep a reference to the intermediate, and dispose it only
when Subset() hands back a new instance.

    var image = FromEncodedData (data);
    if (image == null)
        return null;

    var result = image.Subset (subset);
    if (result != image)
        image.Dispose ();

    return result;

Output is unchanged; the only behavioral difference is that the intermediate is
now released deterministically instead of at finalization.

Add Pr3997ResourceLeakTest to lock this in:

  * FromEncodedDataWithSubsetDoesNotLeakIntermediateImage - the regression guard.
    It inspects the HandleDictionary registry and asserts only the returned
    subset stays registered after the call. Verified red on the old one-liner
    (Expected: 1, Actual: 2 - the leaked intermediate) and green on the fix. It
    runs in the serialized HandleDictionary threading collection so the
    alive-instance count is read in xUnit's non-parallel phase.
  * FromEncodedDataWithSubsetMatchesManualDecodeThenSubset and
    FromEncodedDataWithFullBoundsSubsetReturnsFullImage - parity guards proving

4422.title: Add a daily workflow to track artifact and native binary sizes
4422.body:
Add a daily workflow to track artifact and native binary sizes (#4422)

Context: https://aka.ms/skiasharp-eap/index.json

Package and native-binary sizes drift over time as Skia is updated, but we
had no ongoing visibility into that growth per version or per os/arch. This
adds a scheduled GitHub Actions job that measures the on-disk size of every
SkiaSharp/HarfBuzzSharp NuGet package and each of its native binaries, keeps
a rolling history, and renders a dashboard to the run summary so regressions
are easy to spot.

Two views are tracked across the same 14 columns -- 10 recent daily nightly
builds plus 4 released reference versions:

- All packages: the top-level .nupkg size of every produced package.
- Native packages: the per-os/arch size of each real native binary
  (.so/.dll/.dylib, Apple frameworks, wasm .a), with .pdb symbols excluded
  so the numbers reflect shipped code rather than debug data.

Data sources and approach:

- Nightly is sampled from the official SkiaSharp EAP feed (the aka.ms link
  above, an anonymous Azure DevOps Artifacts v3 feed), taking the latest
  `*.*.*-nightly.*` build. Because SkiaSharp (4.x) and HarfBuzzSharp (14.x)
  version independently, each family's headline nightly is resolved
  separately and every package is measured at its own family's version.
- The 4 released reference roles (prev-major, prev-stable, curr-stable,
  latest) are resolved per package from NuGet.org, measured once, and cached.
- Native packages are auto-detected by scanning nupkg contents, so no package
  list is hard-coded; the family is enumerated from the feed's search service.

Implementation notes:

- .github/scripts/track-artifact-sizes.py -- collector (Python 3, stdlib
  only). Merges into a JSON history: nightly appended and trimmed to 10 days,
  released versions measured once and cached.
- .github/scripts/render-artifact-sizes.py -- renders the history to
  $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY; native packages unchanged over the nightly window are
  collapsed, and arch add/drop is surfaced.
- .github/workflows/track-artifact-sizes.yml -- daily cron plus manual
  dispatch, persisting the JSON via the Actions cache using the rolling
  run-id key + restore-keys prefix pattern. No secrets are required.

The job is guarded by `if: github.repository_owner == 'mono'` so it only runs
on the canonical repo, and the raw artifact-sizes.json is also uploaded as a
run artifact for inspection.

4376.title: [performance] Make HarfBuzzSharp.Buffer.AddUtf8(string) allocation-free (pooled UTF-8 encode)
4376.body:
[performance] Make HarfBuzzSharp.Buffer.AddUtf8(string) allocation-free (#4376)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4375

Buffer.AddUtf8(string) encoded the text with Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(utf8text),
which allocates a throwaway byte[] on every call, and then handed that array to
the native add. Its sibling AddUtf16(string) is already allocation-free, and
AddUtf8 sits on the canonical shaping hot path — SKShaper.Shape(string) ->
buffer.AddUtf8(text) -> SKCanvas.DrawShapedText — so the allocation is paid once
per shaped run / per frame for complex-script text.

Encode into a pooled ArrayPool<byte> buffer instead: rent GetMaxByteCount(len)
bytes, pin the string and the buffer, encode once with the unsafe
Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(char*, int, byte*, int) overload, pass the pointer and the
exact encoded byte count to the existing native AddUtf8(IntPtr, int, int, int),
and return the buffer in a finally. hb_buffer_add_utf8 consumes UTF-8 bytes and
copies them synchronously, and both old and new code use the framework's own
Encoding.UTF8, so the same bytes reach native and the shaping result is
bit-identical. Only the method body changes — the public signature is unchanged
(ABI-safe). The unsafe Encoding pointer overloads and ArrayPool<byte> exist on
all TFMs (net462 / netstandard2.0 included), so there is no #if split.

The rented buffer is intentionally oversized (GetMaxByteCount >= actual), so the
exact byteCount returned by GetBytes is passed to native, never utf8bytes.Length.

Edge behaviour is kept identical to the original Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes path,
now without its allocation or an extra branch:

  - null throws ArgumentNullException (explicit guard).
  - empty flows through the pooled path as a no-op: GetMaxByteCount(0) rents a
    small buffer, GetBytes writes 0 bytes, and AddUtf8(ptr, 0, ...) adds nothing
    — mirroring how AddUtf16(string) already handles the empty case.

Measured (BenchmarkDotNet, MemoryDiagnoser, in-process, net10.0, one reused
buffer reset with ClearContents between adds): zero managed bytes allocated on
every input (7-char word, ASCII sentence, 3-byte CJK, mixed paragraph) versus
32-120 B before, and never slower — the small time win comes from a single
GetMaxByteCount + GetBytes scan instead of encoding into a fresh array. The
0-allocation result is the durable claim; absolute ns vary by hardware/TFM.

Correctness is proven by an equivalence suite that compares AddUtf8(string)
against the verbatim original AddUtf8(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(text), 0, -1) path
on both the pre-shape buffer GlyphInfos and the post-shape glyphs / clusters /
advances (after GuessSegmentProperties + Font.Shape), across ASCII, whitespace,
2-byte, 3-byte CJK, decomposed combining marks, 4-byte emoji/surrogate pairs,
mixed scripts, and long strings that exercise larger pooled buffers; plus
explicit null-throws and empty-is-no-op cases grounded in main's behaviour, and
a teeth guard confirming the comparison detects a deliberately-wrong encode.

4408.title: [performance] Remove per-call char[4] allocation in HarfBuzzSharp.Tag.Parse
4408.body:
[performance] Remove per-call char[4] allocation in HarfBuzzSharp.Tag.Parse (#4408)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4407

HarfBuzzSharp.Tag.Parse(string) packed a tag by copying up to four chars into a
freshly allocated char[4] scratch buffer, space-padding the tail, then folding
the low byte of each slot into the uint. That scratch array is allocated on
every call, and tag parsing is hot during OpenType hydration — feature tags
("liga", "kern"), variation-axis tags ("wght", "wdth", "slnt"), and table tags
are often parsed in batches when configuring fonts and shaping features.

Rewrite Parse to read the first four chars directly and pad missing trailing
slots with spaces inline, with no scratch buffer. Packing semantics are
unchanged: null/empty -> Tag.None, short input space-padded, over-long input
truncated to four, and only the low byte of each UTF-16 code unit is kept.

Add an ABI-safe Parse(ReadOnlySpan<char>) overload and have the string overload
delegate to it via tag.AsSpan(), so callers can parse a slice of a larger string
without a substring allocation. The existing string signature is untouched.

This mirrors the already-merged SkiaSharp.SKFourByteTag.Parse optimization
(#4396); Tag is the HarfBuzzSharp sibling that still carried the old char[4]
path. Change is body + additive overload only, so it is ABI-safe.

Measured (BenchmarkDotNet, MemoryDiagnoser, net10.0) on a 22-tag batch: faster
and allocation-free, repeatable across runs. On .NET 10 both rows report zero
managed allocation because the JIT stack-allocates the non-escaping char[4], so
the win there is codegen (dropping the loops, bounds checks, and array
indexing); on net462 / netstandard2.0, which lack object stack allocation, the
old path additionally heap-allocated the char[4] per call, so those TFMs also
lose that allocation. No allocation regression on any TFM.

Correctness is pinned by precomputed [InlineData] constants (input + expected
packed uint) asserted against both the string and span overloads, plus a
verbatim copy of the original char[4] algorithm as a cross-check oracle, a
sliced-span case, null/empty -> None, a ToString round trip, and a teeth guard
proving the equivalence assertions discriminate a wrong value.

4410.title: Fix release-notes classifier that mis-tagged skia-sync PRs as internal
4410.body:
Fix release-notes classifier that mis-tagged skia-sync PRs as internal (#4410)

The release-notes generator (scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-data.py) tags every
merged PR product / mixed / internal by the files it touched, so the Polish phase
can focus on product changes. Automated [skia-sync] submodule bumps — which change
the shipped native Skia — kept coming out `internal` and being dropped from the
notes (e.g. #4382 in 4.151.0-unreleased and #4262 in 4.148.1-unreleased were tagged
internal despite both bumping externals/skia).

~~ Root cause ~~

_files_by_commit() runs `git log --format=%x1e%H --name-only` and parsed each
record by matching a leading \x1e per line. But run() returns stdout.strip(), and
\x1e (the record separator) is whitespace to Python's str.strip(), so the leading
\x1e on the first record was stripped off. git log lists commits newest-first, so
that first, separator-less record is the newest commit in the range — very often
the latest [skia-sync] bump. The startswith("\x1e") check then missed it, its file
list was dropped, and an empty file set falls through to `internal`.

Parse by splitting on \x1e instead, which recovers every record regardless of the
stripped leading separator.

~~ Sharpen the path tiers ~~

While auditing which paths count as what:

  * product stays the strong signal — binding/ + source/ (managed API & Views) and
    externals/skia (the native Skia submodule, with its vendored HarfBuzz). The
    prefix is exact `externals/skia`, not `externals/`, so it no longer sweeps in
    the sibling externals/depot_tools build toolchain or externals/.gitignore.
  * native/ (per-platform build config) shapes the shipped binaries, so it is not
    internal, but a native/-only PR is usually infra rather than an API/behaviour
    change — so it is `mixed` (Polish judges from the title). Covers the shipped
    WinUI native subtree under native/winui/ too.
  * docs (the mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs submodule, mdoc XML that ships as IntelliSense
    docs) moves up from internal to `mixed`. A bump appears in the parent as the
    bare `docs` gitlink, so the prefix is slash-less and does not collide with
    documentation/ (the docs site, which stays internal).

~~ Make the mapping data-driven ~~

The path→tag mapping is no longer hardcoded in the script. It lives in the committed
scripts/infra/docs/release-notes-paths.json — ordered tiers (tag + patterns) plus a
default — the single deterministic place to edit it. _pr_category loads the tiers
(cached) and returns the first tier with a matching file, else the default. Patterns
match by prefix (str.startswith, unchanged behaviour) or, when they contain a glob
metacharacter (* ? [), by fnmatch.fnmatchcase — so paths, prefixes, and wildcards
are all supported. A missing/malformed config is a hard error, never a silent
fallback to a guessed mapping.

Behaviour is identical to the previous hardcoded tuples, verified across the prefix
cases and the real sync/docs/depot_tools PRs. Committed data.json files self-correct
as pages regenerate on the next prepare run; no data.json format bump. The behaviour
spec (documentation/dev/release-notes-and-api-diffs.md) and the release-notes SKILL.md
are updated to match, including the new config file in the inventory.

4388.title: [performance] Read SKShaper glyph results via zero-copy spans
4388.body:
[performance] Read SKShaper glyph results via zero-copy spans (#4388)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4387

SKShaper.Shape(Buffer, float, float, SKFont) read the HarfBuzz shaping results
through buffer.GlyphInfos and buffer.GlyphPositions. Each of those getters
allocates a full array copy of the native glyph buffer — Buffer.GlyphInfos is
GetGlyphInfoSpan().ToArray() and Buffer.GlyphPositions is
GetGlyphPositionSpan().ToArray() — yet the extraction loop reads each element
exactly once. Both copies are pure per-shape waste, and this sits on the
canonical text hot path: SKCanvas.DrawShapedText -> SKShaper.Shape(string) ->
Shape(Buffer, ...), paid once per shaped run / per frame for complex-script or
shaped text.

Read the results through the existing zero-copy GetGlyphInfoSpan() /
GetGlyphPositionSpan() instead of the array getters:

    -var info = buffer.GlyphInfos;
    -var pos = buffer.GlyphPositions;
    +var info = buffer.GetGlyphInfoSpan();
    +var pos = buffer.GetGlyphPositionSpan();

The loop body is unchanged — indexing is identical on ReadOnlySpan<T>. The
buffer outlives the loop and both accessors call GC.KeepAlive(this), so the
spans over native memory stay valid; GlyphInfo / GlyphPosition are blittable,
so the produced Result is bit-identical to the array path. The three real
Result arrays (points / clusters / codepoints) are still built.

Managed C# only — private method body, no public SKShaper API change (ABI-safe),
no native / externals/skia change, rendering output unchanged.

~~ Proof ~~

Benchmark (SKShaperGlyphExtractionBenchmark, BenchmarkDotNet MemoryDiagnoser,
Linux x64 / net10.0, in-process toolchain) over a 3/24/96-glyph batch: ~33-44%
faster with 58-71% fewer bytes allocated per shape, e.g. 96 glyphs
772 ns / 7248 B -> 432 ns / 2112 B. Absolute ns are hardware/TFM-specific; the
ratios are the portable result.

Equivalence test (SKShaperGlyphExtractionTests, 8 cases): span-vs-array accessor
parity plus a ShapeResultMatchesArrayGetterOracle theory (Arabic
content-font.ttf + Latin segoeui.ttf at various offsets) asserting the shipped
Shape Result is bit-identical to an oracle recomputed from the array getters.
Non-vacuous: perturbing Shape (Codepoint + 1) turns the oracle cases red while
the empty-input and raw-parity cases stay green. 15/15 SKShaper tests pass
before and after.

untouched.

Measured on a 22-tag batch (Apple M3 Pro, .NET 10): 148 ns -> 26 ns, ~5.8x
faster. On modern .NET the JIT already stack-allocates the non-escaping char[4],
so the heap-allocation win is realized on runtimes without object stack
allocation (.NET Framework, Mono, WASM, AOT); everywhere the CPU-time win from
dropping the loops and bounds checks still applies.

~~ Tests ~~

The equivalence theory originally computed expected values at runtime from a
verbatim copy of the old char[4] algorithm, and one input used the range
operator ("...\"[..4]). On the .NET Framework test target the range operator
pulls in System.Index/System.Range, which are declared in both HarfBuzzSharp
and mscorlib, producing CS8356 and failing compilation of the whole Tests
(.NET Framework) job.

Replace the runtime oracle with precomputed [InlineData] constants (input +
expected packed uint), asserting both the string and span overloads against the
constant. This removes the range operator (fixing the .NET Framework build) and
makes the oracle immune to drifting alongside the code under test. Coverage
includes null/empty, padding, truncation, >0xFF low-byte truncation, and
surrogate code units.

~~ Review follow-up ~~

After the empty-span guard the length is always >= 1, so the length check on
the first character was dead; read tag[0] directly to drop the redundant branch
(behaviour unchanged, all parity tests still pass).

4389.title: [release-notes] Rebuild generation as a deterministic pipeline
4389.body:
[release-notes] Rebuild generation as a deterministic pipeline (#4389)

Replaces the old "AI polishes a whole .md page" generator — which kept dropping
headings, bare @handles, contributors, and links — with a deterministic JSON core
plus a thin prose surface. Scripts now own every byte of page structure; the agent
writes only prose strings the renderer validates, so those classes of breakage are
structurally impossible. The page is exactly `render(data.json, prose.json)`.

~~ The pipeline: two commands, one flag set ~~

    prepare.sh  →  (agent writes prose.json per page)  →  render.sh
     (network)            (release-notes skill)             (offline)

prepare.sh runs Cake `docs-api-diff` (API-diff tree + co-release-map.json), then
release-notes-data.py (per-page _sources/<version>.data.json facts), then
release-notes-index.py (_sources/index.json: Chrome schedule + live-head set).
render.sh runs release-notes-render.py --all: re-renders every page, prunes stale
-unreleased heads, and rebuilds TOC.yml + index.md from committed JSON, offline.
Both take only --force / --min-version / --max-version; everything is incremental,
so an unforced run skips work whose output already exists (a shipped API diff never
changes) and there is no "notes-only" mode.

~~ Engines co-located; the skill is a thin surface ~~

All three doc engines live together under scripts/infra/docs/ (the Cake api-diff +
mdoc engines and the renamed release-notes-data/-index/-render.py, next to their
shared versions.json). The skill keeps only SKILL.md, samples/, and the two thin
entrypoints prepare.sh + render.sh, which redirect to the engine. This keeps the
skill simple while the real code sits with the other doc engines — until the Cake
api-diff engine can be retired and folded in.

~~ Committed inputs under _sources/ ~~

Every page input is committed beside the page: _sources/<version>.data.json (facts),
.prose.json (the agent's slots), optional .notes.md (manual additions sidecar),
co-release-map.json (the Cake→python HarfBuzz hand-off), index.json, and the
pr-authors.json author cache. data.json is the timestamp-free whole-file
change-detection key, and the committed JSON lets render.sh reproduce every page
byte-for-byte with no network.

~~ HarfBuzzSharp folded into each SkiaSharp page ~~

There is no separate HarfBuzz family (34 pages removed). HB ships inside each
SkiaSharp release, so it renders as a "## HarfBuzzSharp X.Y.Z" section on the
SkiaSharp page with its own API-diff link, derived from the co-release map.

~~ Incremental, scoped Cake api-diff; legacy gate removed ~~

The single docs-api-diff target skips a line whose folder already has an index.md
unless forced, scopes by version range, and writes a merged {skia_line: hb_line}
co-release-map so scoped runs keep prior entries. The old build-pipeline api-diff
gate (its build.cake task + the api_diff stage in azure-templates-stages-test.yml)
is removed as superseded by the skill + workflow.

~~ Preview keys made unique (core-qualified) ~~

Preview/RC keys in data.json — the handle prose maps summaries onto — are now
core-qualified as <core>-<stage><num> (e.g. 4.148.0-rc1, 3.118.0-p1, 1.53.2-gpu1).
This fixes real collisions a review caught on old pages: nonstandard 2016 trains
(Svg 1 / Gpu 1 both keyed m1) and cross-line roll-ups (two Preview 1s both p1)
previously shared one summary. release-notes-data.py now raises on any duplicate
key, and the renderer validates one summary per preview, so a collision can never
silently ship.

~~ Consolidation ~~

  * generate-release-notes.py → release-notes-data.py; generate-release-notes.sh,
    generate.sh, build-data.sh → replaced by prepare.sh + render.sh.
  * generate-api-diffs.sh folded into prepare.sh (it was release-notes-only).
  * pr-authors.json moved into releases/_sources/.
  * references/TEMPLATE.md, grouping.md, review-checklist.md folded into SKILL.md —
    the renderer is the checklist, so there is one instruction file, not four.
  * The workflow prompt was de-duplicated to defer to the skill for the "how",
    keeping only the CI-specific deltas.

~~ Fixes found while validating ~~

  * Cadence double-prepare: a scoped local regen used to need two prepare passes
    because cadence_milestones() read the in-flight Chrome milestones from the
    rendered .md (which build-index runs before). Now derived from the
    _sources/*.data.json written earlier in Prepare, so a single prepare → render
    works.
  * API-diff banner on prerelease-only lines now links both the SkiaSharp and
    HarfBuzzSharp diffs (committing the line's <version>/ folder lets
    release-notes-data.py attach the SkiaSharp link).

~~ Validation ~~

All 1.x–4.x pages were regenerated with this pipeline (default Copilot model for
polish; an A/B run matched the previously-pinned model). Multiple full CI runs are
green (Prepare + agent + detection; safe_outputs fails pre-merge by design because a
feature branch's patch touches protected paths). Incrementality was verified
end-to-end: deleting 4.151.0 and running a no-force `min 4.147.0` CI job regenerated
exactly 4.151.0 plus 4.150.1-unreleased (a real new PR) and skipped 4.147/4.148.

Spec-first: documentation/dev/release-notes-and-api-diffs.md is the behaviour spec;
docs-overview.md, writing-docs.md, and AGENTS.md are synced to the final pipeline.

4382.title: [skia-sync] Merge upstream chrome/m151 bug fixes
4382.body:
[skia-sync] Merge upstream chrome/m151 bug fixes (#4382)

Companion: mono/skia#282
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/98877992a5...cd6e926914
Upstream CL: https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/1288616
Bug: skia:530646115 / Chromium 532103445

Advance the externals/skia submodule (and cgmanifest.json) on main to
mono/skia@cd6e926914, pulling in one upstream chrome/m151 bug fix:

  * Fix Use-After-Free in SubRunAllocator (google/skia@0208108c7a)

Deserializing a corrupt Slug buffer (SlugImpl::MakeFromBuffer) returns
nullptr early and destroys a std::tuple whose member destruction order is
unspecified, so SubRunInitializer freed the backing memory before
~BagOfBytes in the SubRunAllocator read fEndByte out of it -- a
use-after-free read followed by a wild-free/double-free. Upstream replaces
the tuple with a struct that guarantees the allocator destructs before the
initializer frees the memory. This is the same fix already taken to
release/4.150.x in #4379; see mono/skia#282 for the full analysis.

Submodule bump only: cgmanifest.json commitHash tracks the new mono/skia
commit; chrome_milestone (151) and upstream_merge_commit (0208108c7a) are
unchanged (same-milestone sync, no version bump). The upstream change is
internal C++ (src/text/gpu/SubRunAllocator.h) with no C API or binding
impact -- binding regeneration produced zero diff and the full
SkiaSharp.Tests.Console suite passed (5614 passed, 0 failed, 182 skipped)
on Linux x64.

4377.title: Teach memory-leak-fixer to use SKObject keep-alive helpers instead of hand-rolled fields
4377.body:
Teach memory-leak-fixer to use SKObject keep-alive helpers instead of hand-rolled fields (#4377)

Context: documentation/dev/memory-management.md
Related: #4372, #4355

SkiaSharp already has a built-in mechanism for the "root a related object so
the GC can't collect it while its owner lives" problem: SKObject's static
`Referenced(owner, child)` (backed by the per-object `KeepAliveObjects`
dictionary), plus `Owned`/`OwnedBy` (backed by `OwnedObjects`) for the
root-and-dispose case. `Referenced` is used idiomatically by SKDocument,
SKColorSpace, and SKSVG — but it was never documented in the authoritative
memory-management model, and the memory-leak-fixer skill's area 5 taught a
hand-rolled `private readonly` field (or a `List<T>`) instead.

Because the guidance never pointed at the real feature, recent generated leak
fixes reinvented it: #4372 hand-rolled a `List<SKCanvas>` plus a field, and
#4355 added a `private readonly SKRegion` field. This PR closes that gap so
future runs reach for the framework mechanism instead.

Changes:

  * documentation/dev/memory-management.md — new "Keeping Related Objects
    Alive" section documenting Referenced / Unreferenced / UnreferencedAll and
    Owned / OwnedBy, and the KeepAliveObjects vs OwnedObjects dictionaries
    (roots-only vs roots-and-disposes).
  * memory-leak-fixer/references/types-of-leaks.md — area 5 now teaches
    `Referenced(this, parent)` as the idiomatic fix, with the mutable-set
    variant (`Unreferenced` / `UnreferencedAll`); keeps a plain field as an
    accepted local-convention fallback (e.g. the SKRegion iterators) to avoid
    mixed styles; updates the Where-to-look / How-to-find-it / Watch-out notes.
  * memory-leak-fixer/SKILL.md — self-review gate now flags a hand-rolled
    keep-alive field/List<T> where the helpers suffice.

Docs/skill only — no binding code changes here. The symmetric inverse helpers
(`Unreferenced`, `UnreferencedAll`) that the docs reference are introduced and
consumed in #4372; #4355 consumes the pre-existing `Referenced`.

4380.title: Skip Xcode version validation in MAUI integration test builds
4380.body:
The integration test harness generates throwaway MAUI apps in a temp directory
outside the repo, so they don't inherit tests/Directory.Build.props (which sets

recommends (e.g. Xcode 26.3 vs workload 26.2), before SkiaSharp was ever exercised.

for the generated Apple apps too. Release-testing validates SkiaSharp rendering,
not toolchain version matching. The property is harmless (ignored) on Android.

4361.title: [skills] Add performance-fixer skill + make the benchmark harness AI-ready
4361.body:
[skills] Add performance-fixer skill + make the benchmark harness AI-ready (#4361)

Context: dotnet/aspnetcore optimize-aspnetcore-performance (reference architecture)
Related: #4241 (SKMatrix native→managed, up to 24×), #4345 (SKColor alloc-free parse),
         #4247 (SKSurface.Canvas caching), #4362 (perf/* label taxonomy), #4330 (memory-leak-fixer)

SkiaSharp is a thin managed wrapper over native Skia, so its recurring, high-impact
performance family is the tax the C# layer adds between the caller and Skia — a P/Invoke
transition paid for math that is a few float ops, an allocation on a hot parse/convert
path, a native lookup redone on every getter, or per-element marshalling in a loop. We
have merged several such wins by hand (#4241, #4345, #4247); this adds an autonomous
scanner so more of them surface as code lands, without a human hunting for them.

Add a `performance-fixer` skill (sibling to `memory-leak-fixer`) plus a scheduled gh-aw
workflow that scans the managed binding for one hot-path opportunity, proves it, fixes it
(managed-only, ABI-safe), and files a linked issue + draft PR.

The defining discipline is two proofs, which a generic perf pass lacks: every fix must be
shown FASTER (a BenchmarkDotNet New-vs-Old measurement) AND behaviour-IDENTICAL (an
equivalence test — bit-exact vs SkiaApi.sk_* for numeric ports, across edge inputs, and
mutation-checked to prove it catches divergence). A faster answer that differs from Skia is
a rendering regression, not a win, so it is rejected. The skill also encodes the traps we
learned the hard way: the x86/x87 float-determinism native fallback (#4241), the ARM64
Vector256 regression, statistical benchmark rigor, and full behaviour parity including
exceptions, ownership/GC.KeepAlive lifetime, and rendered pixels.

~~ Reference structure ~~
References are split by area (mirroring the aspnetcore skill): references/hot-paths/*
(SkiaSharp code areas — geometry-math, color, handles-and-collections, text-and-fonts,
pixels-and-images) and references/bcl-patterns/* (the .NET techniques), plus
decision-framework.md (impact×complexity rubric + the two-proof gate), measuring.md,
signals.md (detection routing), and repo-helpers.md. A lean SKILL.md routes between them.

~~ Benchmark harness readiness ~~
So a scan never wastes time repairing infra: replace TheBenchmark.cs — a trap whose
[SimpleJob(Net48/Net70/Net80)] attributes silently skip off-Windows and whose empty bodies
taught none of the conventions — with a working TemplateBenchmark.cs (New-vs-Old +
[MemoryDiagnoser] + [Params] + return-sink that runs out of the box), and add
benchmarks/README.md documenting the add/run commands, --list flat / --job short for fast
iteration, the single-TFM rule, and the InternalsVisibleTo native-oracle pattern.

~~ Labels ~~
Findings are labelled tenet/performance plus one agent-chosen perf/* sub-type from the
shared taxonomy in .agents/skills/issue-triage/references/labels.md (#4362), matching the
memory-leak-fixer convention; the sub-type is decided by the win's dominant measured driver
(a removed P/Invoke → perf/interop, removed allocations → perf/allocations, ...).

~~ Validated end to end ~~
The workflow self-tests on any PR touching the skill via a forced dry-run. Those runs
correctly rejected a non-finding (SKFourByteTag's char[4] is already stack-allocated by
.NET 9/10 escape analysis) and found real, fully-proven wins (SKShaper glyph-array
extraction → perf/allocations; SKColor→SKColorF operator → perf/interop). A real dispatch
run created a correctly-labelled issue (#4369) and draft PR (#4370), confirming the
tenet/performance + perf/* labels land on both.

No binding/runtime code changes: a new skill, a new workflow, benchmark docs/template, and
two rows in AGENTS.md.

4364.title: [release-notes] Banner scaffold + floor-line baseline fix (enable fully-CI regeneration)
4364.body:
[release-notes] Fix the stable banner and floor-line baseline to unblock CI regeneration (#4364)

Two source-only fixes that let the release-notes pipeline regenerate every page
through CI without a human hand-editing output or committing generated content.
Both were found while trying to land the one-time raw-data "format 2" rollout: the
automated bot PR kept failing, and the manual fallback needed hand-fixups — symptoms
of two real defects in the generator, not the polish.

~~ Scaffold the stable banner (the hand-fixup) ~~

The reworked skill requires a themed, dated banner on every page:

    > **<theme>** · Released <date> · [NuGet](…) · [GitHub Release](…)

But of all the banner variants the script emits, the stable one was the only bare,
theme-less placeholder — `> [NuGet](url)`. So on stable pages the polish AI had to
build the entire banner from scratch (theme + date + both links) while every other
status got a ready scaffold: the most work with the least help. A bare-but-valid
NuGet link also "looks done", so a tired pass shipped it, and the prose rules (rule 7
+ self-review + checklist) still missed 2 of 16 pages. Prose alone was not reliable;
the fix had to be structural.

generate-release-notes.py now scaffolds the stable banner like every other status:
the release date (from the vX.Y.Z tag, already computed for the raw-data `released:`
field) and both links are filled in, leaving only a literal `<THEME>` token for the
AI to replace with a 2-4 word phrase. A leftover `<THEME>` is a greppable review
failure, unlike a bare NuGet link that masquerades as finished. On the next CI run
3.116.0 and 4.148.0 came out correctly themed on their own ("First stable v3/v4
release") — no manual edits.

~~ Resolve the floor line's baseline from below the history floor (the churn) ~~

The opt-in history floor (which skips regenerating the obsolete 1.x/2.x
back-catalogue) regressed the API diff of the lowest emitted line. The floor strips
every below-floor line from the emit set, so the floor line (3.0.0) had no baseline
to diff against: no `compare_to` override, and its natural predecessor (2.88.9) was
filtered away. It fell through to a null baseline and the comparer diffed 3.0.0
against an empty 0.0.0.0 assembly, re-emitting its ENTIRE public API as "New Type" —
3.0.0/SkiaSharp/SkiaSharp.md went from a correct "3.0.0.0 vs 2.88.0.0" diff (2688
lines) to a wrong "vs 0.0.0.0" one (5187 lines), rewritten on every run. That churn
is a large subtree, and it is what pushed the format-2 rollout patch over gh-aw's
1024 KB create-pull-request limit.

A baseline may legitimately live below the floor — the spec already promises it
("baselines are unaffected: 3.116.0 still diffs against 2.88.9"), and 3.116.0 works
only because it has an explicit compare_to; the floor line relied on the implicit
predecessor the floor removed. api-diff.cake now splits the computation into
`emittable` (the emission rules) and `emit` (emittable minus the floor). When a line
has no emitted predecessor — i.e. it is the floor line — its baseline is resolved
from `emittable` below it and downloaded for comparison only; it is never emitted
itself, and it is one already-cached package (also the next line's baseline), so the
floor's performance win is preserved. 3.0.0 now regenerates to its correct "vs
2.88.9" diff, matching what is committed, so it drops out of the patch entirely.

~~ Result: fully-CI regeneration ~~

With both fixes, a validation run's bot patch dropped to 741 KB — under the 1024 KB
limit — and every stable page came out correctly banered with no hand edits. The
only remaining failure was gh-aw's protected-files guard tripping on these very
skill/script changes, which resolves once they are in main. After this merges, the
scheduled CI run produces a content-only patch that clears both the size and
protected-files guards and opens the "[docs]" bot PR automatically — the format-2
page rollout and all future regenerations land through CI, with no manually committed
generated files.

Validated the Cake engine still compiles via
`dotnet cake --target=docs-api-diff-past --dryrun`. Spec §1.4 and §4.4 and the
versions.json floor comment document the below-floor baseline resolution and the
script-owned banner scaffold.

4365.title: docs: close the version milestone on every release (not just stable)
4365.body:
docs: close the version milestone on every release (not just stable) (#4365)

cadence — `X.Y.Z-preview.N`, `X.Y.Z-rc.N`, and `X.Y.Z` (stable). The

4362.title: [skills] Add perf/* label taxonomy and rework memory-leak-fixer focus areas
4362.body:
[skills] Add perf/* label taxonomy and rework memory-leak-fixer focus areas (#4362)

Two related improvements to the agentic-workflow skills. Memory-leak
findings previously landed with only the `agentic-workflows` label — a
label read by nothing and present on zero issues/PRs — so leaks and
performance reports had no meaningful classification, and the triage
skill had no rule mapping either to a quality tenet.

~~ perf/* label taxonomy ~~

There is no dedicated "memory-leak" label, and grouping every speed,
memory, or size concern under the single `tenet/performance` umbrella
loses the sub-type. Add a `perf/*` axis beneath that umbrella, grounded
in the repo's real corpus (61 tenet/performance + ~25 memory-leak

perf/rendering, perf/throughput, perf/startup, perf/size. Any perf/*

    SKILL.md, and the report template.
  * auto-triage workflow: apply classification.perf[] labels; raise the
    add-labels cap 10 -> 12 to fit the new axis.

Type classification (type/bug vs type/enhancement) is left to triage on
purpose — a leak is usually a bug, but a "make it faster" report may be
an enhancement.

~~ "family" -> "focus area" rework ~~

Align the memory-leak-fixer's vocabulary with the new performance-fixer
skill (#4361), which routes over "focus areas" and a focus_area knob.
The 11 rotating leak categories are now focus areas rather than
families, and the workflow's focus_family dispatch input is renamed to

4347.title: [release-notes] Rework the polish pipeline into a curated product changelog
4347.body:
[release-notes] Rework the polish pipeline into a curated product changelog (#4347)

The auto-generated release-notes pages had drifted into an exhaustive repository
activity log: one bullet per PR, internal CI/tooling work surfaced next to real
API changes, bare @handles, bot credits, and a plain "> [NuGet]" banner. For a
NuGet consumer opening a version page, the signal they came for was buried. This
PR reworks the Prepare + Polish pipeline so each page reads like a curated
product changelog, and — crucially — makes the quality *deterministic* where an
LLM was previously re-deciding it from scratch every run (the source of the
run-to-run variance).

The work is spec-first: documentation/dev/release-notes-and-api-diffs.md is the
behavior spec and was changed ahead of the generator and skill in every case.
The split of responsibility is deliberate — generate-release-notes.py structures
the raw-data block and stamps deterministic hints; the Polish AI only writes
prose, guided by the skill + references, never re-litigating classification.

~~ Product over project, made deterministic ~~

Rather than ask the AI "is this consumer-facing?" per PR, Prepare now tags every
raw-data PR line by the files it touched, and Polish trusts the tag:

  * [product]  — touches shipped code (binding/ externals/ source/); written up.
  * [internal] — touches none of those (CI, workflows, our .agents/** skills,
                 docs site, tests, samples); collapsed into one trailing line.
  * [mixed]    — touches only build config (native/): may change the shipped
                 binary via a compile define, or be pure infra. Polish guesses
                 from the title/context already in the block (it does NOT open
                 the PR) and surfaces only genuine shipping changes.

native/ is intentionally NOT treated as shipped code — the code that actually
ships is externals/skia/ — so a native compile-flag fix (e.g. the small-sigma
raster-blur regression, SK_AVOID_SLOW_RASTER_PIPELINE_BLURS) lands as [mixed] and
is surfaced by inspection instead of being hidden or blindly promoted.

~~ Curate and group, don't enumerate ~~

The skill was restructured router-style: SKILL.md carries the rules and points at
references/ that the one agent loads on demand — grouping.md (a countable density
budget: ~8-15 grouped bullets total, at most ~4 per category, Breaking Changes
exempt) and review-checklist.md (a 12-point self-review rubric, also runnable
standalone to grade a finished page). Related PRs now merge into thematic bullets
instead of one-per-PR.

~~ Deterministic contributor roster ~~

The credits table was reconstructed ad-hoc from the body prose, so any
contributor whose PRs were folded into a thematic bullet was silently dropped —
4.148.0 listed only 2 of 5 community members and omitted @ramezgerges entirely
(the biggest external v4 contributor, 16 PRs). Prepare now emits an authoritative
`contributors:` roster (every external, non-bot author + their PR numbers) and
Polish renders exactly one row per entry. Bots (github-actions[bot], Copilot,
dependabot, any *[bot]) and the maintainer are excluded at the source, and the
[community ✨] marker is stripped from bot lines so Polish can't invent a
❤️ @Copilot inline credit either.

~~ Banner, and a bounded Highlights ~~

Every page gets a themed, dated, linked banner
("> **<theme>** · Released <date> · [NuGet](…) · [GitHub Release](…)"), with the
release date resolved deterministically from the vX.Y.Z tag. Highlights is now a
hook, not a summary: it had ballooned to a single 228-word paragraph that
re-listed the whole page. The rule is now a mechanically checkable word cap
(target ~80, hard cap 100) under a mandatory `## Highlights` heading, with the
enumeration patterns that caused the bloat explicitly banned — because a
"2-3 sentences" rule alone is trivially gamed by long comma-run sentences.

~~ Rollout plumbing: format version + history floor ~~

Two mechanisms keep the above maintainable across the full back-catalogue:

  * A raw-data `format:` version folded into the idempotent content key. The
    "skip unchanged" check keyed only on data (PR count, diff range, supersession,
    companion hashes), so a quiet line with no new PRs kept its old-format page
    forever — e.g. 4.150.0 stayed on the pre-three-way format with no roster.
    Bumping _RAWDATA_FORMAT_VERSION now rolls a new raw-data format onto every
    page in a single --all run, then settles back to idempotent.
  * An opt-in per-family history floor (versions.json) that skips regenerating
    obsolete lines (1.x/2.x) without deleting their committed pages or affecting
    baselines — a performance skip of the back-catalogue on every automated run.

Validated by dispatching the real update-release-notes pipeline against this
branch and inspecting the polish output: across 16 pages the mechanical checks
are clean (0 bare @handles, 0 bot credits, every page has Breaking Changes and a
## Highlights heading ≤ 100 words), 4.148.0's Highlights dropped 228 → 84 words
with all 5 contributors credited, and 4.150.0's [mixed] blur fix is surfaced
under Fixes.

4356.title: Add focus_family override input to memory-leak-fixer workflow

Add focus_family override to memory-leak-fixer workflow (#4356)

Changes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/compare/main...dev/memory-leak-fixer-focus-override

The "Fixer - Memory Leak" agentic workflow picks which leak family to deep-scan
via a time-based round-robin (day-of-year + hour, mod 11). That keeps unattended
runs varied, but it also means any *one* family only gets a deep scan when the
clock happens to rotate onto it — roughly once every 11 hours. There was no way
to point the scanner at a specific family on demand, which made it hard to
exercise the finding-issue -> fix-PR pairing end to end while iterating.

The first real run (28829268499) made this concrete: its focus landed on

finalizer/collection-ordering family that covers the SKRegion iterators.

  * When set to a bare number, Step 1 passes it to the skill's Phase 1.1, which
    now honors an explicit override and skips the round-robin.
  * When blank (schedule / pull_request / dispatch without it), the rotation is
    unchanged.
  * Independent of `dry_run`, so `focus_family=5 dry_run=false` can force a real
    run on a chosen family.

expressions: gh-aw auto-wires `GH_AW_GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_FOCUS_FAMILY` onto the
