4330.title: Add memory-leak-fixer skill + self-testing agentic workflow
4330.body:
Add memory-leak-fixer skill + self-testing agentic workflow (#4330)

Context: https://github.com/dotnet/maui/pull/36276

Adapts MAUI's AI leak-scanner idea to SkiaSharp's actual leak surface — native
ownership/disposal correctness (undisposed SKObject handles, wrong `owns:` flags,
C-API ref-count mismatches, same-instance double-dispose, unremoved view/handler
subscriptions, `fixed`-pointer lifetime) rather than MAUI's managed view-retention
leaks. Everything is scoped to managed C# (binding/**, source/SkiaSharp.Views*/**);
upstream Skia under externals/skia/** is out of scope.

Two deliverables plus registration:

- .agents/skills/memory-leak-fixer/SKILL.md (+ references/types-of-leaks.md):
  a reusable scan -> prove -> fix methodology grounded in
  documentation/dev/memory-management.md, with an 11-family leak catalogue as the
  single source of truth (each family carries a description, why it leaks, a generic
  example, the idiomatic fix, anti-patterns, and where to look). Golden rule: every
  fix is proven red->green — the regression test must fail without the fix and pass
  with it — before anything ships. Tests are never weakened or muted; generated
  files and upstream Skia are never touched.

- .github/workflows/memory-leak-fixer.md (+ compiled .lock.yml): a gh-aw workflow
  (Copilot / claude-opus-4.8) that runs the skill on a 12h schedule. Every run does
  the same thing — hunt one leak (round-robin family focus by day-of-year + hour),
  prove it, fix it, then emit a linked pair of safe outputs: a `[memory-leak]`
  finding issue and a draft fix PR whose body ends with `Fixes #<temporary_id>`.
  gh-aw resolves the temporary id to the real issue number within the same run, so
  merging the PR auto-closes the finding. The only knob is `dry_run` (do everything
  but open nothing).

- AGENTS.md: registers the skill as /memory-leak-fixer in the command and issue
  classification tables.

The workflow self-tests: any PR that edits the workflow or skill re-runs the whole
pipeline in forced DRY-RUN, emitting only a `noop` (never a real issue/PR), so the
prompt/skill can be iterated on and watched live without side effects. Verified
across several dry-runs — all green, all noop-only. The scanner already surfaced a
genuine finding on otherwise-hardened code: SKRegion.SpanIterator does not root its
parent SKRegion the way its RectIterator/ClipIterator siblings do, a real
use-after-free risk. It is deliberately left unfixed here so the workflow has a real
target to find and fix on its first scheduled run.

4345.title: Optimize SKColor hex parsing and add ReadOnlySpan<char> overloads
4345.body:
[SkiaSharp] Optimize SKColor hex parsing and add ReadOnlySpan<char> overloads (#4345)

SKColor.Parse/TryParse sit on hot paths for code that hydrates colors from
XAML/CSS/JSON/theme files, but the old implementation parsed each channel with
byte.TryParse and the 6/8-digit forms with uint.TryParse (culture + NumberStyles
overhead), and carried a #if split where the net4x/netstandard2.0 path allocated
a `new string(char, 2)` per channel.

Replace that with a single allocation-free parser over ReadOnlySpan<char>
(Trim().TrimStart('#') + a length switch feeding small case-insensitive nibble
helpers), removing the #if split so one implementation serves every TFM. The
core now operates on a span, so re-basing to index 0 also lets the JIT drop the
per-access bounds checks in the fixed-length cases.

Add public span overloads so callers can parse a color out of a larger buffer
without allocating a substring:

    public static SKColor Parse (ReadOnlySpan<char> hexString);
    public static bool TryParse (ReadOnlySpan<char> hexString, out SKColor color);

The existing string overloads delegate to these via AsSpan(), matching the
pattern already used in SKFont, SKTextBlob, and friends. These are pure
additions, so the change is ABI-safe.

Behavior is preserved for every input the old code accepted, with one
intentional tightening: whitespace directly after '#' in the 6/8-digit forms
(e.g. "# 12345") was previously accepted as a side effect of
NumberStyles.HexNumber's AllowLeadingWhite and is now rejected, matching the
stricter behavior the 3/4-digit path already had. Parsing stays
case-insensitive.

This is a pure-managed change with no interop: SKColor is a readonly struct
wrapping a single uint, and neither the parse methods nor the private
TryParseNibble/TryParseByte helpers call into native Skia (no SkiaApi/sk_*,
DllImport/LibraryImport, Marshal, or stackalloc/fixed). No C API or generated
bindings are touched, so no native rebuild is required.

Measured on net10.0 (Apple M3 Pro, BenchmarkDotNet), zero allocations and
~1.4-2.3x faster across all shapes: "#FFF" 8.4ns -> 3.8ns, "#FFFF" 9.4ns ->
4.0ns, "#FFFFFF" 7.0ns -> 4.8ns, "#FFFFFFFF" 8.9ns -> 6.0ns, and invalid
fast-reject 3.7ns -> 1.7ns.

Adds SKColorTest coverage (whitespace, case-insensitivity, null/empty,
named-color rejection, span overloads, slice parsing) plus benchmark projects
documenting the strategy shootout, the span-vs-string comparison, and the
public New-vs-Old numbers.

4340.title: [tests] Add cross-backend golden-image (visual regression) test harness
4340.body:
[tests] Add cross-backend golden-image (visual regression) test harness (#4340)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4295
Supersedes: #4236 (that draft will not be merged; this PR replaces it)
Extracted-from: #3968 (the in-flight Graphite backend PR)

Our tests assert on API behavior and pixel-level spot checks, but nothing
systematically verified that the actual rendered output is correct across
backends. A change in Skia, a driver, or our bindings could silently alter
rendered pixels on one backend (GL/Metal/Vulkan) while every existing test
stayed green. This harness closes that gap: it renders deterministic scenes
through every available backend and diffs each result against a committed
golden PNG with a strict per-renderer tolerance, turning "did this change the
way things draw?" into an automatic, reviewable signal on every PR.

The harness was lifted out of the Graphite backend PR (#3968), which carried
its own ad-hoc visual infra, and reworked into a clean, reusable harness on
main so #3968 can rebase and add only its Graphite renderer classes + golden
PNGs — no new test/CI/infra.

Design (tests/Tests/SkiaSharp/Visual/):
  * Each (renderer x scene) pair is one xUnit theory cell. Scenes and renderers
    are reflection-discovered from catalogs, so adding a scene covers every
    backend and adding a backend covers every scene.
  * Runs in-process inside the runners we already ship — Console (desktop),
    Devices (MAUI: Android/iOS/Mac Catalyst) and Wasm (browser) — with no
    separate render-host app or external orchestration. Package-gated backends
    (Vulkan -> SharpVk, Direct3D -> Vortice) live in the existing satellite host
    projects so that dependency never reaches the MAUI/WASM builds.
  * Failure discipline: a cell skips only when the backend is genuinely absent
    (no device/driver/context); everything else is a hard failure, including an
    unseeded cell that rendered but has no committed golden. No path downgrades
    a real regression to a skip.
  * Goldens resolve {renderer}.{platform}/{scene}.png then the shared
    {renderer}/{scene}.png, and are seeded by harvesting the PNG markers every
    cell emits into the TRX (scripts/infra/tests/extract-visual-goldens.py) —
    the one output channel uniform across desktop, device and browser hosts.
  * CI (scripts/azure-templates-stages-test.yml) provisions headless software
    GL/Vulkan (Xvfb + Mesa llvmpipe/lavapipe) on the Linux agent and republishes
    failing cells as browsable actual/golden/diff PNGs; the matrix runs inside
    the existing test stages, no dedicated visual stage.

Seeded here: raster (shared 4 scenes + per-platform Text for every OS),
ganesh-gl.macos and ganesh-metal.{macos,ios,maccatalyst} for all 5 scenes.
Also fixes the Text scene rendering blank, the embedded-golden lookup for
renderer names with dashes on MAUI/WASM hosts, and a GC-test finalization-chain
flake surfaced by the added tests.

Verified locally on macOS arm64: raster (5/5) and ganesh-metal (5/5) pass with
0 skips and real captured PNGs in the TRX; the remaining desktop-GPU and
device/WASM goldens are seeded per platform from their own CI lanes.

Context: documentation/dev/release-notes-and-api-diffs.md (the behavior spec)

The release-notes polish TEMPLATE lived in the rendered docs tree at
`documentation/docfx/releases/TEMPLATE.md`, where it needed a dedicated DocFX
exclude and sat far from the skill that actually consumes it. It had also drifted
from SKILL.md as the breaking-change guidance grew: the example still used a tiny
`## New Features` -> `### Platform` shape and a 3-row Platform Support table, while
real polished pages are built from top-level `## Category` sections with a fuller
platform table and a linked contributors table. That drift was a contributing
factor in the recent full-render regression, where pages lost their Platform
Support and linked Community Contributors tables.

Move the template to `.agents/skills/release-notes/references/TEMPLATE.md` so it
lives with its skill as a proper reference asset (matching the repo's existing
`references/` convention, e.g. pr-commit-message/references/pryor-style-guide.md),
and remodel its worked example so every section is shown at least once.

@octobot), fake PR numbers, and placeholder dependency versions. This keeps the
template from asserting real facts, avoids falsely attributing invented work to
real contributors, and prevents the polish AI from copying template specifics into
a real page. SKILL.md now calls it a "representative (fictional) example" and tells
the AI to match structure/tone but never copy the placeholders.

  * spec: record the template's new home in the skill-directory tree (§3, now with a
    `references/` subfolder) and in the "division of responsibility" pointer (§4.4).

4343.title: [release-notes] Slim breaking-change guidance to restore the full page render
4343.body:
Context: the good, rich render (4.148.0 @ #4224) predates the breaking-change
initiative and had 9 sections incl. Platform Support and a Community Contributors
table with 21 linked handles. The last three release-notes commits regressed it.

Over #4334 → #4337 → #4341 the breaking-change guidance grew large and became
triplicated — spec §4.7 (four long bullets), SKILL.md companion-rules (five long
bullets), and SKILL.md step 6 (a 13-line paragraph), plus a 20-line TEMPLATE.md
comment — all repeating the same "size to the break / itemize vs. sweep / open
every file / never degrade to silence" machinery.

None of that removed the good-render rules: TEMPLATE.md and SKILL.md still require
Platform Support and a linked Contributors table ("ALWAYS link [@user](url); never
write bare @user"). But the polish is a single agentic pass over ~29 pages, and the
lopsided emphasis (breaking reinforced dozens of lines; Platform Support zero lines
in the skill) crowded out the rest. The render degraded progressively and
systemically: this run dropped Platform Support and the Contributors table on every
sampled page (3.116.0 / 3.119.4 / 4.147.0 / 3.0.0 → 0 Platform Support, 0 contributor
tables, 0 linked handles), collapsing pages to Highlights + Breaking + bare-@handle
prose.

Fix: collapse the breaking guidance to a lean four-rule shape, applied consistently
spec-first (spec → TEMPLATE → SKILL):

  1. Manual notes (.notes.md) — merge neatly; the only channel for behavioral and
     interop breaks the signature diff can't see.
  2. Breaking diff (.breaking.md) — open every listed file, summarize as a few
     bullets, link the API diff for the exhaustive list.
  3. Summarize, don't transcribe.
  4. Always emit the ## Breaking Changes section.

This keeps everything that works — the .notes.md / .breaking.md companion model, the
content-key hashing, and the claude-opus-4.7 Polish pin are all untouched — and only
removes the over-weighting so the single-pass AI treats every section evenly again.
A few-bullet summary also lists exhaustive-itemization corner cases (the source of
the recent SKGRVkImageInfo / Handle nits) less prone to hallucination.

Net: -92 lines removed / +49 added across the three surfaces; no generator or
workflow changes.

4341.title: [release-notes] Never drop the Breaking Changes section; size it to the break
4341.body:
Context: run 28683166739 (bot/release-notes @ a93930782a0)
Regression-from: #4337

The strengthened polish guidance in #4337 ("open every .breaking.md, turn
every distinct entry into a bullet, drop nothing") backfired on bulk breaking
sweeps. In the first production run under that wording the polish AI dropped the
`## Breaking Changes` section entirely on 23 of the 24 pages that have breaking
companions — keeping it only on 4.148.0, the one page with a .notes.md sidecar.
3.116.0 is the clearest case: it *had* a correct grouped bullet

  - Obsolete 2.x APIs are gone in 3.x — upgrading from 2.88 may require source
    changes. (#2539)

and the run deleted it (the commit diff shows `-## Breaking Changes`). The agent
log shows the AI never opened a single 3.116.0 .breaking.md; faced with an
all-or-nothing "itemize every entry, drop nothing" instruction it could not
satisfy for a 1090-line [Obsolete] cull across 12 assemblies, it skipped the
companions and omitted the section — violating the "always include" rule sitting
right above it.

The fix is graceful degradation. The maximalist "itemize everything / nothing
dropped" framing is replaced with size-to-the-break guidance, applied
spec-first (§4.7) then mirrored into the skill and template:

  * Never drop the heading. Omitting the section is the one thing that is never
    acceptable; when itemizing is infeasible, degrade to a grouped summary plus
    a diff link, never to silence.
  * Size the summary to the break. Itemize a small/curated set (a handful of
    entries) with migration snippets; group + summarize + link the API diff for
    a bulk mechanical sweep (the pre-3.0 [Obsolete] cull, a dropped TFM) instead
    of trying to list hundreds of members — a grouped summary is the complete,
    correct answer there.
  * Opening the breaking files stays mandatory, but a skim (wc -l + headings) is
    explicitly enough for a large one, so the AI never has an excuse to skip it.

Files:
  - documentation/dev/release-notes-and-api-diffs.md §4.7 (spec, first)
  - .agents/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md (companion table, companion rules, step 6)
  - documentation/docfx/releases/TEMPLATE.md (Breaking Changes comment)

After merge, re-polish the existing breaking pages (they re-polish this run
regardless while the breaking backfill is unmerged) and confirm 3.116.0's
grouped Breaking bullet returns.

4337.title: [release-notes] Itemize breaking diffs during polish; add 4.148.0 notes sidecar
4337.body:
Context: documentation/dev/release-notes-and-api-diffs.md §4.7
Builds on: #4334 (companion-files model for release-notes polish)

The companion-files model landed in #4334 taught the polish AI to *read* each
`.breaking.md`, but the guidance was soft ("not required to enumerate every
changed member"), and in practice the AI reduced `## Breaking Changes` to a link
to the diff plus a list of PR titles. So the actual diff entries never reached the
page: 4.148.0's breaking section links SkiaSharp.breaking.md but never itemizes
the GRVkImageInfo retype, the GrVkYcbcrConversionInfo value-equality removal, or
the SKNativeObject setter removal it contains.

Two classes of break are also invisible to the signature diff entirely and so can
only reach the notes through the manual sidecar:
  - behavioral changes — same signature, different runtime behavior (e.g.
    new SKPaint().Typeface now returns Default instead of null); and
  - interop / native structs outside the public-API surface the diff compares
    (e.g. the five GRVkBackendContextNative fields removed for #3741), which show
    up in no *.breaking.md at all.

~~ Strengthen the polish phase (spec-first) ~~

  * Spec §4.7: the AI must OPEN every listed .breaking.md and turn each concrete
    entry into prose — a link is not a substitute for reading it, and PR titles
    are not a substitute for the diff's entries. Every distinct break must be
    represented (grouped/summarized, not dumped). Adds the behavioral +
    interop-struct channel and frames diff and sidecar as complementary.
  * SKILL.md: companion table + rules + step 6 reworded to "itemize, don't just
    link"; calls out the breaks that never appear in any .breaking.md.
  * TEMPLATE.md: Breaking Changes comment now says OPEN and itemize every
    breaking file; link/PR-titles are not substitutes; fold in the sidecar's
    behavioral/interop breaks.

~~ Validated 4.148.0 manual sidecar ~~

  * documentation/docfx/releases/4.148.0.notes.md documents the seven v4
    behavioral/interop breaks (#3734–#3738, #3740, #3741) that the signature diff
    cannot show, with before/after and migration snippets lifted from the issues.
    Freeform Markdown; the generator (unchanged here) discovers it, folds its hash
    into the content key so an edit re-polishes only that page, and lists it in the
    raw block's companions manifest. Partly closes #3683.

No generator or native changes; docs/skill/sidecar only.

4334.title: release-notes: manual notes sidecar + AI-summarized breaking changes
4334.body:
release-notes: manual notes sidecar + AI-summarized breaking changes (#4334)

Two tied capabilities for the spec-driven release-notes system, plus a
refinement to how the API-diff / breaking companions are surfaced. This
closes a real gap: behavioral breaking changes (same signature, different
runtime behavior — e.g. `new SKFont()` now carries an empty typeface,
`SKPaint().Typeface` returns Default instead of null) never appear in a
signature diff, so today they reach the notes through no channel at all.

~~ Manual additions sidecar (`<stem>.notes.md`) ~~

A maintainer-authored, freeform-Markdown sidecar co-located with a
version's hub page. It is never machine-overwritten: the generator hashes
its bytes into the page content key (`notes:`) and the Polish AI reads and
weaves it into the prose, so it survives `--branch` / `--all` regeneration
and re-polish. This is the durable home for behavioral breaks and for any
point a maintainer simply wants brought out — not all of it is "breaking".
The file is docfx-excluded and discovery-guarded, so it is never treated
as a version page or emitted into the TOC.

~~ AI-summarized breaking changes (companion model) ~~

The page's raw-data block now references companion files by path + hash
rather than embedding them, and the Polish AI opens and summarizes them
into a `## ⚠️ Breaking Changes` section:

  * API diff → a single `index.md` entry: the version folder's landing
    page that links every per-assembly diff and flags the breaking ones.
  * API breaking diff → one `- breaking:` line per broken assembly, folded
    into one order-stable combined `breaking:` hash. Paths keep their
    package-folder prefix so identically-named files (e.g.
    `SkiaSharp.Views.Windows.breaking.md` under both `Uno.WinUI/` and
    `WinUI/`) stay distinct. A major release like 3.116.0 enumerates all
    twelve.

~~ Behavior and rollout ~~

The content key (`_is_content_unchanged`) now folds in the `notes:` and
`breaking:` hashes, so a companion-only edit re-polishes exactly that page
and everything stays idempotent. On the first `--all` run, the 25 pages
that predate the feature but carry a breaking diff gain the `breaking:`
manifest + section as a one-time backfill; unaffected pages are skipped.

Validated end-to-end via a `source_branch` dispatch of the Sync workflow
(run 28677098312): Prepare + Polish ran green off this branch's scripts +
skill, re-polished exactly the 25 breaking-bearing pages, and wrote correct
`## Breaking Changes` prose for 3.116.0 (12 companions) and 4.148.0 (1).

Spec-first order, matching the repo rule: spec (§3.7 sidecar, §4.7
companions) → generator → docfx exclusion → TEMPLATE.md → SKILL.md →
workflow (Polish pinned to a stronger model for companion summarization).

The Pages Deploy workflow builds a full ~470 MB staging preview (DocFX +

4313.title: [docs-site] Sweep staging previews for open PRs inactive over 3 months
4313.body:
[docs-site] Sweep staging previews for open PRs inactive over 3 months (#4313)

Context: .github/workflows/build-site-cleanup-stale.yml

The "Pages - PR Staging - Sweep Stale" workflow garbage-collects per-PR
documentation preview folders under `staging/<pr_number>/` on the
`docs-live` branch. Previously it only removed a folder once its PR was
CLOSED or MERGED, so long-lived open PRs kept their staging previews
indefinitely and the branch accumulated stale directories forever.

Add an inactivity-based rule as a first step: an open PR's staging folder
is now also swept when the PR has not been updated in longer than
`STALE_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (default 90 days / ~3 months). "Older than 3 months"
is intentionally interpreted as last-activity (`updatedAt`) rather than
creation date, matching the intent of reclaiming untouched previews. The
sweep now queries `state,updatedAt` via `gh pr view`, and PRs that cannot
be resolved (deleted / transient API failure) are explicitly left in
place so a flaky API call can never trigger a wrong deletion.

Guard the force-push retry path against the new rule. Because staleness
now depends on `updatedAt`, an open PR could be updated and its preview
redeployed while the sweep is running; the previous retry loop only
checked directory existence and could delete the freshly redeployed
folder after losing the `--force-with-lease` race and resetting to the
new `docs-live`. The staleness decision is extracted into an `is_stale()`
helper used by both the initial scan and the retry loop, so each
candidate is re-queried live before removal and a PR that became active
again is kept.

- Threshold is configurable via the `STALE_MAX_AGE_DAYS` env var.
- Uses GNU `date -d` and `jq`, both available on `ubuntu-latest`.

4306.title: [skia-sync] Drive upstream sync from versions.json with a run-number rotation
4306.body:
[skia-sync] Drive upstream sync from versions.json with a run-number rotation (#4306)

Context: scripts/infra/docs/versions.json (support.stable / support.preview)

The daily Skia upstream sync tracked milestones off a fixed mode map — three
crons resolving to `current` (main's milestone), `next` (+1) and `latest`
(highest upstream chrome/m*), plus dispatch-only `main`. That map never covered
the lines we actually ship: the supported stable maintenance lines (e.g.
release/4.148.x and release/4.150.x) only received bug-fix syncs when a human
manually dispatched them by number, so they silently drifted from upstream.

Make the sync self-describing instead. A single `0 */6 * * *` cron now ROTATES
over the hand-maintained `support` block in versions.json: each run syncs one
line — stables ascending, then previews ascending — plus a trailing `next`
(highest supported milestone + 1), which becomes a real milestone bump into main
when upstream has cut chrome/m<next>, or the upstream main tip (skia-sync/main)
when it has not. Coverage now follows versions.json automatically as lines are
added or retired.

The trigger surface collapses to one dispatch input `target`: empty = rotate,
`main` = upstream tip, or a milestone number (e.g. 151) = explicit sync. The old
`mode`/`milestone` inputs and the current/next/latest modes are removed.

~~ Keeping the two detector passes in agreement ~~

The detector (.github/scripts/skia-sync-detect.sh) runs twice per workflow run —
the pre_activation `--gate` pass and the agent-job "align submodule" pass — in
separate jobs that cannot share outputs. A GPT-5.5 review flagged three ways
those passes could diverge and align a different branch/submodule than the gate
approved. All three are closed:

  * the round-robin index is GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER % len, which is identical across
    every job of a run — no wall-clock read, so no chance of the two passes
    landing on different targets near a time boundary;
  * main's milestone and the support block are read at the immutable GITHUB_SHA
    rather than the mutable branch ref, so a mid-run push to main cannot change
    what the second pass sees;
  * chrome_branch_exists fails hard on a git ls-remote error instead of treating
    a transient failure as "branch absent" and silently falling back to main.

A supported line older than main's milestone with no matching release/*.x branch
is now skipped (nowhere valid to sync) rather than merged into main.

~~ Fix update-versions.ps1 writing a literal ref in tip mode ~~

Surfaced while validating the main-tip path: Phase 6's update-versions.ps1
resolved the merged upstream commit with a hardcoded
`git rev-parse "upstream/chrome/m$Target"`. On a main-tip sync the merged ref is
`upstream/main`, so `upstream/chrome/m<Target>` does not exist — and plain
`git rev-parse` on a missing ref echoes the literal argument to stdout and exits
non-zero. The guard was only an empty-string check, so the literal string
`upstream/chrome/m151` was written into cgmanifest.json's upstream_merge_commit
as if it were a SHA. Add an optional `-UpstreamRef` parameter (default
chrome/m<Target>), resolve with `git rev-parse --verify --quiet
"upstream/<ref>^{commit}"` + $LASTEXITCODE so a missing ref fails cleanly to
UNKNOWN, and pass `-UpstreamRef "${upstream_ref}"` from the workflow.

.github/workflows/auto-skia-sync.lock.yml is regenerated by `gh aw compile`; do
not edit it by hand. (gh-aw materializes the prompt body at runtime, so the
markdown-body edits here don't change the lock — only frontmatter does.)

Validated by dispatching the workflow against this branch: a rotate run
(deterministically resolved to the main-tip line) and an explicit target=151 run.
Both passes agreed on the target, produced the correct skia-sync/main and
skia-sync/m151 branch pairs, and finished green (native + C# build clean, tests
5584 passed / 0 failed). Those throwaway validation PRs/branches have been closed
and deleted.

single `docs-format-docs` target in scripts/infra/docs/docs.cake (+213). It loads
each type XML once (XDocument), formats it, and runs deterministic checks in the
same pass: warnings for missing/placeholder/quality issues, build-failing errors
only for broken XML/CDATA. build.cake wires the target in.

~~ Obsolete handling ~~
Makes references/obsolete-api-map.md the unambiguous, overload-aware authority and
removes the name-only obsolete-in-example linter. Name matching could not tell an
obsolete overload from a modern one (DrawText/MeasureText exist on both the
deprecated SKPaint forms and the modern SKFont/SKCanvas(..,SKFont,..) forms), so it
produced false positives and a skill that contradicted its own reference. Obsolete
judgement is now the reviewer's, guided by the map (the deprecated overload is the
one without an SKFont parameter).

Validated by two CI runs of the companion workflow (PRs #168 and #169): consistent
across both — 8 placeholders filled source-first, 23 lint findings fixed, 0 final
findings, no obsolete usage introduced, no valid modern SKFont/SKCanvas overloads
deleted, and MS Learn OpenPublishing Errors:0.

4284.title: Add embedded image/font selectors to SkiaFiddle
4284.body:
Add embedded image/font selectors to SkiaFiddle (#4284)

Context: https://fiddle.skia.org/ ("Optional source image")

The in-browser SkiaFiddle playground had no way to draw real images or
interesting fonts: a snippet could only paint procedurally. This adds a
preloaded asset library plus a toolbar so snippets can use a picked image
and typeface directly, mirroring skia.org/fiddle's source-image feature.

Assets are embedded, not downloaded. The trimmed Release WASM build strips
HttpClient's download methods, so runtime fetching is impossible; instead
six canonical Skia fiddle source images (1.png-6.png, from the Skia
buildbot repo) and four fonts (Inter variable, Nabla COLR/CPAL color,
DejaVu Serif, DejaVu Sans) are bundled and loaded at startup. Provenance
and licenses are recorded in samples/SkiaFiddle/Media/README.md (BSD-3
images; OFL / Bitstream-Vera fonts).

A new toolbar exposes a font ComboBox and a Skia-drawn image thumbnail
strip (ImageStripCanvas, wrapped in a transparent Border for pointer
hit-testing). The current selection is injected into every snippet as the
`image` and `typeface` variables, read live each frame so switching updates
the next frame without recompiling. Three demo samples exercise this:
source image, variable font (wght axis), and color font (palettes), each
carrying per-sample font/image hints.

Trimming/build issues surfaced and fixed during validation:

  * Formatted interpolation in snippets - preserve
    System.Runtime.CompilerServices.DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler in
    ILLink.Descriptors.xml. The in-browser Roslyn compiler binds against the
    trimmed runtime assemblies, where the format-bearing AppendFormatted
    overloads were removed, so any snippet using $"{x:0}" failed with CS1739.
  * Asset double-publish - a build target strips embedded Media/ from
    Content. Uno's default **\*.png glob pulls them into Content, and Release
    resets DefaultItemExcludes so a property-based exclude doesn't take.
  * Obsolete DrawText - bundled samples use the non-obsolete SKTextAlign
    overload (was CS0618).

The bundled samples were also tidied for readability: brief section
comments, snippet bodies wrapped to ~80 columns with inner constructions
(gradient colour arrays, sampling options, text coordinates) hoisted into
named locals to avoid horizontal scrolling, and the sample picker sorted
alphabetically by category. Wrapping is confined to the snippet strings
shown in the editor; the surrounding C# stays on normal single lines.

Validated end-to-end against the trimmed Release WASM build (published
locally, driven with Playwright): the toolbar renders, image/typeface swap
live, the color font shows real COLR/CPAL palettes, the variable font
animates its wght axis, the dropdown is confirmed sorted, and all nine
bundled samples compile warning-free and render. All changes are scoped to
samples/SkiaFiddle/ - no binding, native, or C-API changes.

4282.title: [Infra] Add milestone sync and audit scripts for Chrome-aligned releases
4282.body:
[Infra] Add milestone sync and audit scripts for Chrome-aligned releases (#4282)

SkiaSharp's v4 release cadence is aligned 1:1 with Chrome milestones:
Chrome Beta → Preview.1, Early Stable → Preview.2, Stable Cut → RC,
Stable → Stable. Maintaining milestones manually across 4 releases per
Chrome version is error-prone and tedious.

Add two PowerShell scripts under scripts/infra/milestones/:

sync-chrome-milestones.ps1 — fetches the Chromium release schedule from
chromiumdash.appspot.com and creates/updates GitHub milestones with
correct due dates and descriptions. Reads the current milestone number
from scripts/VERSIONS.txt. Idempotent and safe to run on a schedule.

audit-milestones.ps1 — verifies that merged PRs and their linked issues
are assigned to the correct milestone by computing git merge-base ranges
between consecutive release branches. Uses GraphQL
closingIssuesReferences for sidebar-linked issues and regex for body
keywords. Reports mismatches and optionally fixes them.

Both scripts support -DryRun, handle pagination (--paginate --slurp),
use UTC throughout, sort milestones in proper release order (not
lexicographic), and check $LASTEXITCODE on all API calls.
